classification.difficultyReason: Requires a five-stage angle argument using two isosceles triangles and supplementary angles, with a reason for every stage.

content.prompt: Show that $\angle BAD = 80^{\circ}$. Give a reason for each stage of your working.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle ABC with D on AC and BD drawn. Single ticks identify AB = AD; double ticks identify BD = DC. Ordinary source strokes are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: A, D and C are collinear in that order; AB = AD; BD = DC; angle BCD = 25 degrees. Coordinates are derived from these relationships and are not printed measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 25-degree angle, vertex labels and equality marks appear in the question figure.

answer.short: $\angle DBC=25^{\circ}$, $\angle BDC=130^{\circ}$, $\angle ADB=50^{\circ}$ and $\angle DBA=50^{\circ}$, so $\angle BAD=80^{\circ}$.

inlines.text: (base angles of isosceles triangle BDC are equal, since BD = DC).
(angles on a straight line sum to 180°).
(base angles of isosceles triangle ABD are equal, since AB = AD).
(angles in a triangle sum to 180°), as required.
